SMTO-CFG-0046 — SMTO's shutdown wait time must be above zero

GUID: 19efb281-2201-4d38-b8f2-75f55576be30
Slug: config-runtime-worker-join-timeout-seconds-must-be
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • A startup setting tells SMTO how long to wait for its background work to stop when it shuts down, but it is set to zero or less, so SMTO stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the settings file (usually config.yaml) in a plain text editor and find worker_join_timeout_seconds under the runtime section. That line sets how long SMTO waits for background work to stop.
  2. Change it to a positive number of seconds, or delete the line to use the standard 2 seconds. Then start SMTO again. With zero or less, SMTO would have no time to stop its background work cleanly.
  3. If SMTO still stops with this message, make sure you edited the file SMTO really uses: the one given after --config when it was started, or config.yaml in SMTO's own folder. SMTO may be reading a different copy of the settings file than the one you changed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the message from the window where SMTO was started) and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change other timeouts or limits to work around this; only the shutdown wait time is wrong.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration validation failed because runtime.worker_join_timeout_seconds in the application YAML is zero or negative.

What this means

  • The structured runtime section sets worker_join_timeout_seconds to zero or a negative duration. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • The structured runtime section sets worker_join_timeout_seconds to zero or a negative duration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the worker-join setting, distinct from task execution and model request deadlines.

How to fix it

  • Set runtime.worker_join_timeout_seconds in the bootstrap YAML to a positive number of seconds, or omit it for the 2-second default; it bounds how long shutdown waits for each execution worker to stop. AOR_WORKER_JOIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS overrides the effective value later; a nonpositive environment value is rejected by Settings and reported as SMTO-CFG-0062, not this error.
  • Set runtime.worker_join_timeout_seconds to the intended positive shutdown-wait duration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported positive worker-join duration passes startup validation.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
